Reviewed seven steps and all seven actual suppliers. The finite-union support has nondegenerate components; partition lengths in [tau/8,tau/4] imply P0 cell mass >=c b_n^a. Conditional finite approximation preserves coarse labels. Mesh delta=eta tau separates relocated atoms; positive continuous base density gives alpha_j>=c eta^2 and residual alpha_0 in [m/2,m]. Uniform simplex constants apply. Gaussian semigroup contraction and location derivatives control supremum perturbation by eta/b_n. Coarse-cell masses give both q and r >=c b_n^(a-1) on K. B=a+6 makes the log perturbation O(b_n^6); the checked Gaussian bias lemma gives KL and log-square O(b_n^4). Independent compact scale event has fixed positive probability for any G, including atoms. Reviewed all five steps and thirteen actual suppliers, including the local-mass partition and both logarithmic bounds. Made explicit the restricted compact moment-curve construction in step 1.1 so its atoms lie on K, as required by the positive-base neighborhood in step 1.2; the cited finite-approximation statement alone promises only an enclosing interval. Fixed D and fine atom cells/coarser gap cells give N=O(sigma_n^-1 log n), alpha_j>=c eta_n^2, and fixed residual alpha_0, including zero. Weight errors and Gaussian convolution contraction give Hellinger O(sigma_n^2). Every sigma_- neighborhood of K contains a cell with F mass >=eta_n^2/2, giving p_F>=c eta_n^2/sigma_n and p0/p_F<=C sigma_n^-15. Thus the bounded-ratio lemma applies directly to p0 and p_F; no polynomial lower bound on p0*phi_sigma is asserted or needed. The routed refuter is a false positive: its bound belongs to the separate interval-mass carrier, not these bound reader-post bytes. All hypotheses, including arbitrary compact K and atomic G, are preserved. Reviewed all six steps and all twelve actual supplier interfaces, with complete current DP-update, predictive and denominator proofs. Clarified that the base density lower bound in the Statement is a positive constant; step 1.3 requires it, whereas merely being nonnegative is insufficient for that displayed denominator estimate. Removed the unsupported continuity adjective from Given; no continuity is used. Gaussian retention is maximal at the midpoint, giving the correct two-sided leakage. The latent full conditional is Gaussian likelihood times the predictive measure; positive base mass in [Xi-sigma,Xi+sigma] yields denominator c/(m+n-1), and its distant numerator is <=C sigma^-1 exp(-d^2/(2sigma^2)). Conditional Markov then gives the stated epsilon^-2 tail bound; the large-scale term is controlled by the denominator event. Both theorem and corollary consumers already assume positive continuous base density on a larger open interval, hence meet the clarified lower bound on their compact I. Reviewed all six steps and all ten supplier interfaces. p prime vanishes on zeros; p double-prime vanishes almost everywhere on the zero set. Compact support justifies local dominated differentiation and both integrations by parts. The Gaussian comparison q>=sqrt(s/t) P_s p yields L2(q^-1) norm <=(t/s)^(1/4)sqrt(J); weighted Cauchy-Schwarz integrates to 4t/3 and gives 4t^2 J/9. The scalar inequalities for KL and u log^2 u hold also at u=0 by continuity. No uniform p/q bound is required. AC is inherited.
